Provided here for ergonomic imports.\npub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Outcome {\n    Outcome::classify(exit_code, was_interrupted)\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// OutcomeHandler\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Routes agent outcomes to their explicit handlers.\npub struct OutcomeHandler {\n    config: Config,\n    telemetry: Telemetry,\n}\n\nimpl OutcomeHandler {\n    pub fn new(config: Config, telemetry: Telemetry) -> Self {\n        OutcomeHandler { config, telemetry }\n    }\n\n    /// Run a bead store operation with a 30s timeout.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Ok(Some(T))` on success, `Ok(None)` on timeout, and `Err(E)` on\n    /// other errors. Callers should treat timeout and error as non-fatal — log\n    /// and continue rather than blocking the worker in HANDLING state.\n    async fn timeout_op<T, F, Fut>(\n        &self,\n        op: F,\n        operation_name: &str,\n    ) -> Result<Option<T>, anyhow::Error>\n    where\n        F: FnOnce() -> Fut,\n        Fut: std::future::Future<Output = Result<T, anyhow::Error>>,\n    {\n        match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), op()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(result)) => Ok(Some(result)),\n            Ok(Err(e)) => Err(e),\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    operation = operation_name,\n                    \"bead store operation timed out after 30s\"\n                );\n                Ok(None)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Release a bead with sync conflict recovery and graceful failure handling.\n    ///\n    /// Flow:\n    /// 1. processing other beads even if release fails.\n    async fn release_bead(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead: &Bead) -> Result<Vec<EventKind>> {\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        // Step 1: Flush local writes to JSONL before attempting release.\n        // Emit heartbeat before br call to track where hang occurs.\n        let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted {\n            bead_id: Some(bead.id.clone()),\n            state: \"HANDLING_FLUSH\".to_string(),\n        });\n\n        match self.timeout_op(|| store.flush(), \"flush\").await {\n            Ok(Some(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"flushed local changes to JSONL before release\"\n                );\n                // Emit heartbeat after successful flush.\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted {\n                    bead_id: Some(bead.id.clone()),\n                    state: \"HANDLING_FLUSH_DONE\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"flush timed out before release, attempting release anyway\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"release\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"flush\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"flush failed before release, attempting release anyway\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"release\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"flush\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Attempt release with timeout protection.\n        // Emit                // Emit heartbeat after successful release.\n                let _ = self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::HeartbeatEmitted {\n                    bead_id: Some(bead.id.clone()),\n                    state: \"HANDLING_RELEASE_DONE\".to_string(),\n                });\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadReleased {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n this is a SyncRecoveryError (sync recovery was attempted but failed).\n                if e.downcast_ref::<SyncRecoveryError>().is_some() {\n                    tracing::error!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"br release failed after SYNC_CONFLICT recovery — \\\n                         worker will continue (bead may              \"br release failed — worker will continue (bead may remain assigned)\"\n                    );\n                }\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    reason: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                // Timeout after 30s.\n                tracing::error!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"br release timed out after 30s — worker will continue (bead may remain assigned)\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    reason: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(events)\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a process output for the given bead.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `classify()` to determine the outcome, then dispatches to the\n    /// per-outcome handler. self.telemetry.emit_try_lock(EventKind::OutcomeHandled {\n            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            outcome: outcome.as_str().to_string(),\n            action: bead_action.to_string(),\n tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", outcome.as_str());\n        }\n\n        Ok(HandlerResult {\n            outcome,\n            bead_action,\n            telemetry_events,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Handle a process output with cancellation support.\n    ///\n    /// Checks the cancellation flag before starting the handler and returns\n    /// early was_interrupted),\n                bead_action: BeadAction::None,\n                telemetry_events: vec![],\n            });\n        }\n\n        // Wrap the handler in a timeout to prevent indefinite hangs.\n        // This is a safety net in case the internal br call timeouts don't work.\n        // Configurable via `validation.outcome_timeout_seconds` (default 50) —\n        // see let bead_id = bead.id.clone();\n        let telemetry = self.telemetry.clone();\n        let timeout_secs = self.config.validation.outcome_timeout_seconds;\n\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs),\n            self.handle(store, bead, output, was_interrupted),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(result)) => Ok(result),\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                // Handler returned an error.\n                tracing::error!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    error = %e,\n tracing::error!(\n                    bead_id = %bead_id,\n                    timeout_secs,\n                    \"outcome handler timed out, returning early to allow worker recovery\"\n        outcome: classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted)\n                        .as_str()\n                        .to_string(),\n                    operation: \"handle\".to_string(),\n                    error: format!(\"timeout after {}s\", timeout_secs),\n                });\n                // Return a default HandlerResult to allow the worker to recover.\n                // The worker's 60-second timeout wrapper will handle best-effort release.\n                Ok(HandlerResult {\n                    outcome: classify(output.exit_code, was_interrupted),\n                    bead_action: BeadAction::Released,\n                    telemetry_events: vec![EventKind::BeadReleased {\n                        bead_id,\n                        reason: \"handler_timeout\".to_string(),\n                    }],\n                })\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Success: run validation gates (if configured), then verify bead closure.\n    ///\n    /// Flow:\n    /// 1. If all gates pass (or none configured): check if agent closed the bead.\n    ///    - Closed → emit BeadCompleted.\n    ///    - Still open → emit BeadOrphaned warning.\n    ///\n    /// NEEDLE does NOT auto-close — the agent owns closure via `br close`.\n    async fn handle_success(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent completed successfully\");\n\n        // Try pluggable gates first, fall back to legacy verification commands.\n        let gate = if !self.config.gates.is_empty() {\n            // New pluggable gate system. Fill in each command gate's stderr\n            // cap from `validation.stderr_cap_bytes` unless the gate already\n            // set its own override — see GitHub issue jedarden/NEEDLE#9.\n            let default_stderr_cap = self.config.validation.stderr_cap_bytes;\n            let gate_configs: Vec<(String, GateConfig)> = self\n                .config\n                .gates\n                .iter()\n                .enumerate()\n                .map(|(i, config)| {\n                    let mut config = config.clone();\n                    let GateConfig::Command {\n                        stderr_cap_bytes, ..\n                    } = &mut config;\n                    if stderr_cap_bytes.is_none() {\n                        *stderr_cap_bytes = Some(default_stderr_cap);\n                    }\n                    (format!(\"gate_{}\", i), config)\n                })\n                .collect();\n            ValidationGate::new(gate_configs, bead.workspace.clone())\n        } else if !self.config.verification.is_empty() {\n            // Legacy verification command format.\n            ValidationGate::from_commands_with_stderr_cap(\n                self.config.verification.clone(),\n                bead.workspace.clone(),\n                self.config.validation.stderr_cap_bytes,\n            )\n        } else {\n            None\n        };\n\n        if let Some(gate) = gate {\n            let report = gate.run(bead).await?;\n\n            if !report.all_passed {\n                return self.handle_gate_failure(store, bead, &report).await;\n            }\n\n            // All gates passed — emit telemetry.\n            let gates_run = report.results.len() as u32;\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::VerificationPassed {\n                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                gates_run,\n            })?;\n            tracing::info!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                gates_run,\n                \"all validation gates passed\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        // Reset failure count on successful gate completion.\n        // This ensures the bead starts fresh on the next cycle if re-claimed.\n        let _ = self.reset_failure_count(store, bead).await;\n\n        // Normal success flow: check if agent closed the bead.\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        // Use timeout for show() to prevent indefinite hang in HANDLING state.\n        match self.timeout_op(|| store.show(&bead.id), \"show\").await {\n            Ok(Some(current)) if current.status.is_done() => {\n                if self.config.worker.enforce_shipped_work {\n                    match verify_shipped_work(&current, &bead.workspace, store).await {\n                        Ok(crate::validation::GateResult::Fail(reason)) => {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                reason = %reason,\n                                \"bead closed but shipped-work check failed — reopening and releasing\"\n                            );\n                            let report = GateReport::single_failure(\"shipped_work\", reason);\n                            return self.handle_gate_failure(store, bead, &report).await;\n                        }\n                        Ok(crate::validation::GateResult::Pass) => {}\n                        Err(e) => {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"shipped-work check errored — failing open\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n\n                // Dispatch is fully accounted for — drop its snapshot so the\n                // next claim of this bead starts from a fresh baseline.\n                crate::validation::predispatch::clear(&bead.workspace, &bead.id).await;\n\n                tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"bead confirmed closed by agent\");\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadCompleted {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    duration_ms: 0,\n                });\n                // Increment success_count for any skills that matched this bead.\n                if !bead.workspace.as_os_str().is_empty() {\n                    if let Ok(lib) = crate::skill::SkillLibrary::load(&bead.workspace) {\n                        if let Err(e) = lib.increment_success_for_bead(&bead.labels, &bead.title) {\n                            tracing::warn!(\n                                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                error = %e,\n                                \"failed to increment skill success counts\"\n                            );\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(Some(current)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    status = %current.status,\n                    \"agent exited successfully but bead is still open (orphaned)\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::BeadOrphaned {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                });\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                // Timeout - emit telemetry and continue.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"show() timed out, could not verify bead closure status\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"success\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"show\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"could not verify bead closure status\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"success\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"show\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Flush SQLite state to JSONL so the closed/orphaned bead is captured in\n        // the git-committed backup. Non-fatal: a flush failure is logged but does\n        // not block the worker from picking up the next bead.\n        match self.timeout_op(|| store.flush(), \"flush\").await {\n            Ok(Some(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"flushed bead state to JSONL after success\");\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"flush timed out after success — JSONL may lag SQLite\");\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, error = %e, \"flush failed after success — JSONL may lag SQLite\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::None, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Handle gate failure: reopen the bead if it was closed, then release it.\n    async fn handle_gate_failure(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        report: &crate::validation::GateReport,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        // Find the first failing gate for telemetry.\n        let (failed_gate, reason) = report\n            .results\n            .iter()\n            .find(|(_, r)| !r.passed())\n            .map(|(name, r)| (name.clone(), r.failure_reason().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string()))\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| (\"unknown\".to_string(), \"unknown error\".to_string()));\n\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            gate = %failed_gate,\n            reason = %reason,\n            \"validation gate failed — releasing bead\"\n        );\n\n        // Emit verification failure telemetry.\n        self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::VerificationFailed {\n            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            command: failed_gate.clone(),\n            exit_code: None,\n            output: reason,\n        })?;\n\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        // If the agent already closed the bead, reopen it before releasing.\n        // Use timeout to prevent indefinite hang in HANDLING state.\n        match self.timeout_op(|| store.show(&bead.id), \"show\").await {\n            Ok(Some(current)) if current.status.is_done() => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"reopening bead closed by agent (verification failed)\"\n                );\n                match self.timeout_op(|| store.reopen(&bead.id), \"reopen\").await {\n                    Ok(_) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to reopen bead — attempting release anyway\"\n                        );\n                        events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                            outcome: \"gate_failure\".to_string(),\n                            operation: \"reopen\".to_string(),\n                            error: e.to_string(),\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n            Ok(None) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"show() timed out during gate failure handling, skipping reopen\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"gate_failure\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"show\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"show() failed during gate failure handling\"\n                );\n            }\n            _ => {}\n        }\n\n        // Release the bead back to open with flush-before-release and sync recovery.\n        let mut release_events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        events.append(&mut release_events);\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment the failure count and apply the same\n        // quarantine ceiling `handle_failure` uses. Without this, a bead that\n        // fails a gate every cycle is released back to open forever: the\n        // ARMOR/bf-135k storm ran one bead 24 times in a single day, each\n        // attempt leaving another commit behind. A gate failure is no less\n        // repeatable than an agent failure and must respect the same ceiling.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        let mut action = BeadAction::Released;\n        if release_succeeded {\n            match self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                Ok(new_count) => {\n                    let threshold = self.config.outcome.quarantine_after_failures;\n                    if threshold > 0 && new_count >= threshold {\n                        match self\n                            .quarantine_bead(store, bead, new_count, threshold)\n                            .await\n                        {\n                            Ok(quarantine_events) => {\n                                events.extend(quarantine_events);\n                                action = BeadAction::Quarantined;\n                            }\n                            Err(e) => {\n                                tracing::warn!(\n                                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                    error = %e,\n                                    \"failed to quarantine bead after exceeding gate-failure threshold\"\n                                );\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to increment failure count after gate failure\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add a label indicating verification failure.\n        if let Err(e) = tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, \"verification-failed\"),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                error = %e,\n                \"failed to add verification-failed label\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok((action, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Failure: release bead and increment failure count.\n    ///\n    /// Mitosis evaluation (for multi-task splitting) is handled externally by\n    /// the worker after outcome handling — see `MitosisEvaluator`.\n    ///\n    /// If br calls timeout or fail, logs the error and continues — does not\n    /// block the worker in HANDLING state indefinitely.\n    async fn handle_failure(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent failure — releasing bead\");\n\n        let mut events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment failure count and check the\n        // quarantine threshold. A bead that has exceeded\n        // `outcome.quarantine_after_failures` consecutive failures is\n        // quarantined (status=blocked) instead of being left released-to-open\n        // for the next cycle to re-claim and fail again indefinitely. This\n        // also closes the mitosis `NotSplittable` fallthrough (worker/mod.rs):\n        // that verdict no longer matters for beads at or past the ceiling,\n        // since this check already ran before mitosis evaluation this cycle.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        let mut action = BeadAction::Released;\n        if release_succeeded {\n            match self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                Ok(new_count) => {\n                    let threshold = self.config.outcome.quarantine_after_failures;\n                    if threshold > 0 && new_count >= threshold {\n                        match self\n                            .quarantine_bead(store, bead, new_count, threshold)\n                            .await\n                        {\n                            Ok(quarantine_events) => {\n                                events.extend(quarantine_events);\n                                action = BeadAction::Quarantined;\n                            }\n                            Err(e) => {\n                                tracing::warn!(\n                                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                                    error = %e,\n                                    \"failed to quarantine bead after exceeding failure threshold\"\n                                );\n                            }\n                        }\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"failed to increment failure count after release\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Ensure we emit a reason event for telemetry.\n        if !events.iter().any(|e| {\n            matches!(\n                e,\n                EventKind::BeadReleased { .. } | EventKind::BeadReleaseFailed { .. }\n            )\n        }) {\n            events.push(EventKind::BeadReleased {\n                bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                reason: \"failure\".to_string(),\n            });\n        }\n\n        Ok((action, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Timeout: release bead and add `deferred` label.\n    ///\n    /// If br calls timeout or fail, logs the error and continues — does not\n    /// block the worker in HANDLING state indefinitely.\n    async fn handle_timeout(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent timed out — releasing bead as deferred\");\n\n        let mut events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // If release succeeded, increment failure count and add deferred label.\n        let release_succeeded = events\n            .iter()\n            .any(|e| matches!(e, EventKind::BeadReleased { .. }));\n        if release_succeeded {\n            // Increment failure count for auto-split tracking.\n            if let Err(e) = self.increment_failure_count(store, bead).await {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to increment failure count after timeout\"\n                );\n            }\n\n            if let Err(e) = tokio::time::timeout(\n                std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                store.add_label(&bead.id, \"deferred\"),\n            )\n            .await\n            {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"add_label deferred timed out or failed after timeout release\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"timeout\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"add_label\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Deferred, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Crash: release bead and create alert bead with diagnostic info.\n    async fn handle_crash(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        signal_code: i32,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::error!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            signal_code,\n            agent = %self.config.agent.default,\n            \"agent crashed — releasing bead and creating alert\"\n        );\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n\n        // Create alert bead with diagnostic info (best-effort).\n        let signal_num = if signal_code > 128 {\n            signal_code - 128\n        } else {\n            signal_code\n        };\n        let timestamp = Utc::now().to_rfc3339();\n        let alert_title = format!(\"ALERT: Agent crash on bead {}\", bead.id);\n        let alert_body = format!(\n            \"## Agent Crash Report\\n\\\n             \\n\\\n             - **Bead ID**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Agent**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Exit code**: {} (signal {})\\n\\\n             - **Workspace**: {}\\n\\\n             - **Timestamp**: {}\\n\\\n             \\n\\\n             The agent process was killed. This bead has been released for retry.\",\n            bead.id,\n            self.config.agent.default,\n            signal_code,\n            signal_num,\n            bead.workspace.display(),\n            timestamp,\n        );\n\n        // Hook 4: propagate stitch labels from the crashed bead to the alert.\n        let signal_label = format!(\"signal-{}\", signal_num);\n        let mut alert_labels: Vec<String> = vec![\"alert\".into(), \"crash\".into(), signal_label];\n        alert_labels.extend(crate::types::extract_stitch_labels(&bead.labels));\n        let alert_label_refs: Vec<&str> = alert_labels.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.create_bead(&alert_title, &alert_body, &alert_label_refs),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(alert_id)) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    %alert_id,\n                    \"crash alert bead created\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to create crash alert bead\"\n                );\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"create_bead timed out after 30s during crash handling\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok((BeadAction::Alerted, events))\n    }\n\n    /// AgentNotFound: release bead, emit error. No retry — this is a config issue.\n    async fn handle_agent_not_found(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::error!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            agent = %self.config.agent.default,\n            \"agent binary not found — releasing bead (config issue, no retry)\"\n        );\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        Ok((BeadAction::Released, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Interrupted: release bead for graceful shutdown.\n    async fn handle_interrupted(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n    ) -> Result<(BeadAction, Vec<EventKind>)> {\n        tracing::info!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"agent interrupted — releasing bead for clean shutdown\");\n\n        let events = self.release_bead(store, bead).await?;\n        Ok((BeadAction::Released, events))\n    }\n\n    /// Increment the failure count label on a bead.\n    ///\n    /// Labels follow the pattern `failure-count:N`. If `failure-count:2` exists,\n    /// the old label is removed and `failure-count:3` is added.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the new failure count (or 0 if the operation failed).\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn increment_failure_count(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead: &Bead) -> Result<u32> {\n        // Read labels with timeout.\n        let labels =\n            match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.labels(&bead.id))\n                .await\n            {\n                Ok(Ok(l)) => l,\n                Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"could not read labels to increment failure count\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(0);\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        \"labels() timed out after 30s, skipping failure count increment\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(0);\n                }\n            };\n\n        let current_count = labels\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|l| l.strip_prefix(\"failure-count:\"))\n            .filter_map(|n| n.parse::<u32>().ok())\n            .max()\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n\n        let new_count = current_count + 1;\n        let new_label = format!(\"failure-count:{}\", new_count);\n\n        // Remove old failure-count labels before adding the new one.\n        // Each remove_label call is wrapped in a timeout.\n        for label in &labels {\n            if label.starts_with(\"failure-count:\") {\n                match tokio::time::timeout(\n                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                    store.remove_label(&bead.id, label),\n                )\n                .await\n                {\n                    Ok(Ok(())) => {}\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to remove old failure-count label\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            \"remove_label timed out after 30s\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add the new label with timeout.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, &new_label),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    count = new_count,\n                    \"failure count incremented\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to add failure-count label\"\n                );\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"add_label timed out after 30s\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(new_count)\n    }\n\n    /// Reset the failure count label on a bead by removing all `failure-count:N` labels.\n    ///\n    /// Called on success to clear the failure counter so the bead starts fresh\n    /// on the next cycle.\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn reset_failure_count(&self, store: &dyn BeadStore, bead: &Bead) -> Result<()> {\n        // Read labels with timeout.\n        let labels =\n            match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.labels(&bead.id))\n                .await\n            {\n                Ok(Ok(l)) => l,\n                Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        error = %e,\n                        \"could not read labels to reset failure count\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n                Err(_) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        bead_id = %bead.id,\n                        \"labels() timed out after 30s, skipping failure count reset\"\n                    );\n                    return Ok(());\n                }\n            };\n\n        // Remove all failure-count labels.\n        let mut removed_count = 0;\n        for label in &labels {\n            if label.starts_with(\"failure-count:\") {\n                match tokio::time::timeout(\n                    std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n                    store.remove_label(&bead.id, label),\n                )\n                .await\n                {\n                    Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                        removed_count += 1;\n                    }\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            error = %e,\n                            \"failed to remove failure-count label\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            bead_id = %bead.id,\n                            label,\n                            \"remove_label timed out after 30s\"\n                        );\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        if removed_count > 0 {\n            tracing::debug!(\n                bead_id = %bead.id,\n                removed_count,\n                \"failure count reset\"\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Quarantine a bead by setting status=blocked and adding the 'cycling' label.\n    ///\n    /// This is called when a bead exceeds the configured failure threshold.\n    /// Emits a BeadQuarantined telemetry event.\n    ///\n    /// All `br` calls are wrapped in timeouts to prevent indefinite hang in\n    /// HANDLING state. Failures are non-fatal — we log and continue.\n    async fn quarantine_bead(\n        &self,\n        store: &dyn BeadStore,\n        bead: &Bead,\n        failure_count: u32,\n        threshold: u32,\n    ) -> Result<Vec<EventKind>> {\n        let mut events = Vec::new();\n\n        tracing::warn!(\n            bead_id = %bead.id,\n            failure_count,\n            threshold,\n            \"quarantining bead after exceeding failure threshold\"\n        );\n\n        // Set status=blocked with timeout. This is what actually stops Pluck\n        // from re-selecting the bead — the 'cycling' label below is a\n        // human-facing marker, not the enforcement mechanism.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(30), store.block(&bead.id)).await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(bead_id = %bead.id, \"set status=blocked\");\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to set status=blocked during quarantine\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"block\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"block timed out after 30s during quarantine\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"block\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Add the 'cycling' label with timeout.\n        match tokio::time::timeout(\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),\n            store.add_label(&bead.id, \"cycling\"),\n        )\n        .await\n        {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => {\n                tracing::debug!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"added 'cycling' label\"\n                );\n            }\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"failed to add 'cycling' label\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"add_label\".to_string(),\n                    error: e.to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    bead_id = %bead.id,\n                    \"add_label timed out after 30s\"\n                );\n                events.push(EventKind::WorkerHandlingTimeout {\n                    bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n                    outcome: \"quarantine\".to_string(),\n                    operation: \"add_label\".to_string(),\n                    error: \"timeout after 30s\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Emit the BeadQuarantined event.\n        events.push(EventKind::BeadQuarantined {\n            bead_id: bead.id.clone(),\n            failure_count,\n            threshold,\n        });\n\n        Ok(events)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Outcome Display\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nimpl fmt::Display for Outcome {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self Outcome::AgentNotFound => write!(f, \"AgentNotFound\"),\n            Outcome::Interrupted => write!(f, \"Interrupted\"),\n            Outcome::Crash(code) => write!(f, \"Crash({})\", code),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// Shipped-work verification: did a bead's closure correspond to real,\n//! durable output?\n//!\n//! Gated by `worker.enforce_shipped_work` (default `true`). Runs only when an\n//! agent has already closed the bead (see `outcome::handle_success`). Passes\n//! if either:\n//! - a commit was made since dispatch started (per the `validation::predispatch`\n//!   snapshot) that touches at least one file outside `notes/`/`.beads/`, and\n//!   that commit has been pushed to the upstream remote; or\n//! - the bead's own `notes` field changed during this dispatch — i.e. the agent\n//!   recorded a bead note explaining why no code change was needed.\n//!\n//! With no snapshot the gate has no baseline and **fails open** — it cannot tell\n//! a commit made during the dispatch from one that predates it, and releasing on\n//! \"don't know\" would recreate the retry loop it exists to stop.\n//!\n//! Deliberately does NOT accept a commit touching only `notes/`/`.beads/` as\n//! sufficient on its own: a prior incident (see docs/notes on ARMOR's\n//! commit-storm) showed a worker stuck retrying an uncompletable bead will\n//! happily satisfy a bare \"must have a commit\" rule by committing a trivial\n//! \"still blocked\" doc file every cycle, each one triggering paired CI\n//! version-bump commits. Recording that kind of status belongs on the bead\n//! through the workspace's configured backend, not in git history.\n//!\n//! # Why not `updated_at`\n//!\n//! The original fallback compared `post.updated_at > pre.updated_at`. That is\n//! unsound: `bf close` *is* an update, so the timestamp always advances on the\n//! exact path the gate exists to judge — an agent that closed a bead having\n//! shipped nothing. Combined with a missing snapshot writer, this made the gate\n//! inert from the day it shipped (2026-07-30) until this change: no closure was\n//! ever rejected, and no bead ever received the `verification-failed` label.\n//! Comparing the `notes` field instead keys on a deliberate note update.\n//!\n//! Depends on: `types`, `validation::predispatch`.\n\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\nuse anyhow::Result;\n\nuse crate::bead_store::BeadStore;\nuse crate::types::Bead;\nuse crate::validation::predispatch::{self, hash_notes};\nuse crate::validation::GateResult;\n\n/// Paths that don't count as \"substantial\" on their own. Fail\n    // OPEN. ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// ETXTBSY (\"Text file busy\") occurs when the kernel blocks execution of a binary\n/// that has a write-mode file descriptor still open. This is a genuine race condition:\n///\n/// 1. A process writes a binary to disk and closes the file descriptor.\n/// 2. The kernel's page cache and filesystem synchronization haven't fully completed.\n/// 3. Another process immediately attempts to `exec()` the same binary.\n/// 4. The kernel returns ETXTBSY (errno 26) because the file is still marked for write.\n///\n/// This is most common with:\n/// - Freshly-extracted upgrade binaries executed immediately\n/// - Test fixtures written and chmod'd immediately before use\n/// - Any binary that's written to disk and executed in quick succession\n///\n/// The race is narrow (typically <100ms) but real. Retrying with a short backoff\n/// is the correct fix — the file descriptor is already closed, we're just waiting\n/// for the kernel to finish its internal bookkeeping.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n///\n/// # When to use this helper\n///\n/// Use this wrapper whenever spawning a subprocess that may have been written to\n/// disk immediately before execution:\n///\n/// - Freshly-installed or updated binaries\n/// - Test fixtures created during test setup\n/// - Any executable extracted from an archive and immediately run\n///\n/// Do NOT use this for long-running processes or stable system binaries — the\n/// retry overhead is unnecessary and ETXTBSY is unlikely in those cases.\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use std::path::Path;\n/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry;\n///\n/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/binary\");\n/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n///     || async {\n///         tokio::process::Command::new(binary_path)\n///             .arg(\"--version\")\n///             .output()\n///             .await\n///     },\n///     5,\n///     20,\n/// ).await?;\n/// # Ok(())\n/// # }\n/// ```\npub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry<F, Fut, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    backoff_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n{\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn().await {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms\n                );\n                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms)).await;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting MAX_ATTEMPTS\"))\n}\n\n/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` calls that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned\n/// process (e.g., for timeout handling with `kill_on_drop`).\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>>,\n{\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(spawn_fn, max_attempts, backoff_ms).await\n}\n\n/// Retry wrapper for subprocess spawns with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// This variant uses **exponential backoff** with jitter, making it more suitable for\n/// high-concurrency scenarios where multiple processes might race for the same binary.\n/// Exponential backoff prevents thundering herd problems that linear backoff can cause.\n///\n/// The backoff formula is: `base_ms * 2^attempt + random_jitter`, where:\n/// - `base_ms` is the initial delay (default: 20ms)\n/// - `attempt` is the current retry number (0-indexed)\n/// - `random_jitter` is ±25% of the calculated delay to prevent synchronization\n///\n/// Example backoff sequence with base_ms=20:\n/// - Attempt 1: ~20ms (15-25ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 2: ~40ms (30-50ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 3: ~80ms (60-100ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 4: ~160ms (120-200ms with jitter)\n/// - Attempt 5: ~320ms (240-400ms with jitter)\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\n///\n/// # When to use exponential vs linear backoff\n///\n/// Use exponential backoff when:\n/// - Spawning multiple processes concurrently that might race for the same binary\n/// - Running in high-concurrency environments (CI, parallel tests)\n/// - Dealing with slow filesystems where the race window might be longer\n///\n/// Use linear backoff (`spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry`) when:\n/// - Spawning a single process in isolation\n/// - The race window is known to be very short (<50ms)\n/// - Minimal latency is more important than thundering herd prevention\n///\n/// # Example\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use std::path::Path;\n/// use needle::bead_store::spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential;\n///\n/// # async fn example() -> Result<(), std::io::Error> {\n/// let binary_path = Path::new(\"/path/to/freshly-written-binary\");\n/// let output = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(\n///     || async {\n/// Ok(())\n/// # }\n/// ```\npub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential<F, Fut, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<T>>,\n{\n    use rand::Rng;\n\n    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn().await {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n\n                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n\n                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n                let delay = exponential_delay\n                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    delay_ms = delay,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    delay\n                );\n                tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay)).await;\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n}\n\n/// Retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned process\n/// (e.g., for timeout handling with `kill_on_drop`).\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - An async function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(Child)` - The spawned child process on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub async fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential_child<F, Fut>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> Fut,\n    Fut: std::future::Future<Output = std::io::Result<tokio::process::Child>>,\n{\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(spawn_fn, max_attempts, base_ms).await\n}\n\n// ─── Synchronous ETXTBSY retry helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for subprocess spawns that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// This is the sync equivalent of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry`, using `std::thread::sleep`\n/// instead of `tokio::time::sleep`. Use this for synchronous `std::process::Command` spawns\n/// in non-async contexts.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync<F, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    backoff_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<T>,\n{\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY sync retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(26) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms = backoff_ms,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in {}ms\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    backoff_ms\n                );\n                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(backoff_ms));\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting MAX_ATTEMPTS\"))\n}\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` calls that handle ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `std::process::Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned\n/// process (e.g., for timeout handling) in synchronous contexts.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 5)\n/// * `backoff_ms` - Backoff delay between retries in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(Child)` - The spawned child process on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_child<F>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    backoff_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<std::process::Child>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<std::process::Child>,\n{\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync(spawn_fn, max_attempts, backoff_ms)\n}\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for subprocess spawns with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// This is the sync equivalent of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential`, using `std::thread::sleep`\n/// instead of `tokio::time::sleep`. Use this for synchronous `std::process::Command` spawns\n/// in non-async contexts.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(T)` - The subprocess output on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential<F, T>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<T>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<T>,\n{\n    use rand::Rng;\n\n    const ETXTBSY_ERRNO: i32 = 26;\n    const JITTER_PERCENT: f64 = 0.25; // ±25% jitter\n\n    let mut last_err = None;\n    let mut rng = rand::thread_rng();\n\n    for attempt in 0..max_attempts {\n        match spawn_fn() {\n            Ok(output) => {\n                if attempt > 0 {\n                    debug!(\n                        attempt = attempt + 1,\n                        max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                        function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential\",\n                        \"ETXTBSY sync exponential retry succeeded after {} attempts\",\n                        attempt + 1\n                    );\n                }\n                return Ok(output);\n            }\n            Err(e) if e.raw_os_error() == Some(ETXTBSY_ERRNO) && attempt + 1 < max_attempts => {\n                last_err = Some(e);\n\n                // Calculate exponential backoff: base_ms * 2^attempt\n                let exponential_delay = base_ms * (1 << attempt);\n\n                // Add jitter to prevent synchronization\n                let jitter_range = (exponential_delay as f64 * JITTER_PERCENT) as u64;\n                let jitter = rng.gen_range(0..=jitter_range * 2);\n                let delay = exponential_delay\n                    .saturating_add(jitter)\n                    .saturating_sub(jitter_range);\n\n                warn!(\n                    attempt = attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts = max_attempts,\n                    delay_ms = delay,\n                    function = \"spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential\",\n                    \"ETXTBSY error detected (attempt {}/{}), retrying in ~{}ms (exponential backoff with jitter)\",\n                    attempt + 1,\n                    max_attempts,\n                    delay\n                );\n                std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(delay));\n            }\n            Err(e) => return Err(e),\n        }\n    }\n\n    Err(last_err.expect(\"loop always sets last_err before exhausting max_attempts\"))\n}\n\n/// Synchronous retry wrapper for `Command::spawn()` with exponential backoff for ETXTBSY (errno 26).\n///\n/// Specialized version of `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential` for subprocess spawns that\n/// return a `std::process::Child` process. Use this when you need to interact with the spawned\n/// process (e.g., for timeout handling) in synchronous contexts.\n///\n/// # Parameters\n///\n/// * `spawn_fn` - A function that attempts to spawn the subprocess\n/// * `max_attempts` - Maximum number of retry attempts (default: 10)\n/// * `base_ms` - Base backoff delay in milliseconds (default: 20)\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Ok(Child)` - The spawned child process on success\n/// * `Err(io::Error)` - The last error if all attempts are exhausted\npub fn spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential_child<F>(\n    spawn_fn: F,\n    max_attempts: u32,\n    base_ms: u64,\n) -> std::io::Result<std::process::Child>\nwhere\n    F: Fn() -> std::io::Result<std::process::Child>,\n{\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_sync_exponential(spawn_fn, max_attempts, base_ms)\n}\n\n/// Result of a version check.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum VersionCheck {\n    /// Version is OK or unknown (no known issues).\n    Ok,\n    /// Known-bad version detected with specific issues.\n    KnownBad {\n        version: String,\n        issues: Vec<String>,\n    },\n    /// Version check failed (bf not found, parse error, etc.).\n    Failed { reason: String },\n}\n\n/// Spawn `<br_path> --version>`, retrying briefly on ETXTBSY.\n///\n/// Wraps `spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry` to handle the specific case of checking\n/// bead-forge version. The retry logic handles the race condition where a\n/// binary written to disk moments earlier (e.g., during upgrade or test setup)\n/// transiently reports \"Text file busy\" (errno 26).\nasync fn spawn_version_check(br_path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<std::process::Output> {\n    spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n        || async {\n            tokio::process::Command::new(br_path)\n                .arg(\"--version\")\n                .output()\n                .await\n        },\n        5,\n        20,\n    )\n    .await\n}\n\n/// Check the bead-forge version and detect known-bad versions.\n///\n/// This function runs `bf --version` and parses the output to detect\n/// versions with known bugs. The primary use case is detecting bead-forge\n/// 0.2.0, which has a bug where `--limit 0` returns an empty set instead\n/// of all beads.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// - `VersionCheck::Ok` if the version is not known to be bad\n/// - `VersionCheck::KnownBad` if a known-bad version is detected\n/// - `VersionCheck::Failed` if the version check failed\npub async fn check_bead_forge_version(br_path: &Path) -> VersionCheck {\n    let timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);\n\n    let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout, spawn_version_check(br_path)).await {\n        Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n        Ok(Err(e)) => {\n            return VersionCheck::Failed {\n                reason: format!(\"failed to spawn bf --version: {e}\"),\n            };\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            return VersionCheck::Failed {\n                reason: \"bf --version timed out after 5s\".to_string(),\n            };\n        }\n    };\n\n    if !output.status.success() {\n        return VersionCheck::Failed {\n            reason: format!(\n                \"bf --version exited with code {}\",\n                output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1)\n            ),\n        };\n    }\n\n    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout);\n    let version = stdout.trim().to_string();\n\n    if version.is_empty() {\n        return VersionCheck::Failed {\n            reason: \"bf --version produced no output\".to_string(),\n        };\n    }\n\n    // Extract version number by taking the second word if present\n    // This handles formats like \"bf 0.2.0\" or \"br 0.2.0-github\"\n    let version_number = version.split_whitespace().nth(1).unwrap_or(&version);\n\n    // Check against known-bad version prefixes\n    let mut issues = Vec::new();\n    for &(bad_prefix, issue) in KNOWN_BAD_VERSIONS {\n        if version_number.starts_with(bad_prefix) {\n            issues.push(issue.to_string());\n        }\n    }\n\n    if !issues.is_empty() {\n        VersionCheck::KnownBad { version, issues }\n    } else {\n        VersionCheck::Ok\n    }\n}\n\n/// Run version handshake and emit telemetry for known-bad versions.\n///\n/// This is called during worker boot to detect and warn about known-bad\n/// bead-forge versions. It emits a WARN-level telemetry event if issues\n/// are found.\npub async fn run_version_handshake(br_path: &Path) {\n    match check_bead_forge_version(br_path).await {\n        VersionCheck::Ok => {\n            tracing::debug!(\"bead-forge version check passed\");\n        }\n        VersionCheck::KnownBad { version, issues } => {\n            for issue in &issues {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    version = %version,\n                    issue = %issue,\n                    \"bead-forge version has known bugs — explicit limits will be used to work around\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n        VersionCheck::Failed { reason } => {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                reason = %reason,\n                \"failed to check bead-forge version — cannot detect known-bad versions\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Corruption detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Known error strings that indicate SQLite database is locked (transient).\npub const LOCK_MARKERS: &[&str] = &[\n    \"database is locked\",\n    \"sqlite error: 5\", // SQLITE_BUSY = database is locked\n    \"sqlite error: 6\", // SQLITE_LOCKED = table is locked\n];\n\n/// Known error strings that indicate br sync conflicts.\npub const SYNC_CONFLICT_MARKERS: &[&str] = &[\"SYNC_CONFLICT\", \"JSONL is newer\", \"sync conflict\"];\n\n/// Check if an error message indicates SQLite database corruption.\n///\n/// Returns `true` if the message contains any known corruption marker.\npub fn is_corruption_error(msg: &str) .any(|marker| msg.contains(marker))\n}\n\n/// Check if an error message indicates SQLite database is locked (transient condition).\n///\n/// Returns `true` if the message contains any known lock Examples\n///\n/// ```no_run\n/// use needle::bead_store::has_valid_bead_store;\n/// use std::path::PathBuf;\n///\n/// let workspace = PathBuf::from(\"/home/coding/myproject\");\n/// if SyncRecoveryError {\n    pub reason: String,\n}\n\n// ─── Filters ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Filters applied when listing ready beads.\n#[derive(Debug, body: &'a str,\n    pub labels: &'a [&'a str],\n}\n\n// ─── BeadStore trait ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Abstract interface to the bead backend.\n#[async_trait]\npub trait BeadStore: Send + Sync {\n    /// Whether an error indicates corruption according to this store's backend.\n    fn is_corruption_error(&self, _message: &str) -> bool {\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// Whether an error indicates a transient lock according to this store's backend.\n    fn is_lock_error(&self, _message: &str) -> bool {\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// Whether an error indicates a sync conflict according to this store's backend.\n    fn is_sync_conflict(&self, _message: &str) -> bool {\n        false\n    }\n\n    /// List all beads with no incomplete blockers (ready to work on).\n    ///\n    /// Returns an empty `Vec` when the queue is empty — that is not an error.\n    /// Returns `Err` if JSON parsing or br invocation fails.\n    async fn ready(&self, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>;\n\n    /// List ALL beads in the workspace (no readiness/filter checks).\n    ///\n    /// Used by Knot strand for three-state verification — a DIFFERENT code\n    /// path from `ready()` to avoid v1's false-positive bug.\n    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>>;\n\n    /// Fetch a single bead by ID.\n    async fn show(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead>;\n\n    /// Fetch a bead together with the number of claim-related history entries\n    /// the backend exposed for it.\n    ///\n    /// Most backends do not include event history in their normal bead\n    /// projection, so the default implementation reports no count.  A\n    /// backend that does expose history can override this to let NEEDLE stop\n    /// retrying a bead before another claim mutation grows its JSON record.\n    async fn show_with_claim_history(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<(Bead, Option<u32>)> {\n        Ok((self.show(id).await?, None))\n    }\n\n    /// Fetch operator/agent notes when the backend exposes them.\n    ///\n    /// Backends without a notes projection return `None`; this keeps notes a\n    /// capability rather than forcing it into NEEDLE's common bead model.\n    async fn notes(&self, _id: &BeadId) -> Result<Option<String>> {\n        Ok(None)\n    }\n\n    /// Attempt to atomically claim a bead (set status=in_progress, assignee=actor).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a `ClaimResult` describing the outcome:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)` — success, returns the full bead.\n    /// - `RaceLost { claimed_by }` — another worker got there first.\n    /// - `NotClaimable { reason }` — bead not in a claimable state.\n    async fn claim(&self, id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>;\n\n    /// Atomically find and claim the next available bead (server-selected).\n    ///\n    /// This is the preferred method for multi-worker scenarios as it eliminates\n    /// race conditions: the server selects the bead and assigns it in a single\n    /// BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. Two workers calling this simultaneously will\n    /// always receive distinct beads.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a `ClaimResult` describing the outcome:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)` — success, returns the full bead.\n    /// - `NotClaimable { reason }` — no beads available to claim.\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>;\n\n    /// Release a claimed bead back to open (e.g., after agent failure).\n    async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Quarantine a bead by setting status=blocked (e.g., after it exceeds the\n    /// consecutive-failure threshold in `OutcomeConfig::quarantine_after_failures`).\n    ///\n    /// Unlike `release`, this deliberately does NOT clear the assignee or return\n    /// the bead to a claimable state — the whole point is to stop Pluck from\n    /// re-selecting it until a human (or a future auto-split) intervenes.\n    async fn block(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Clear the assignee on a bead without changing its status.\n    ///\n    /// Used by mend to heal open beads with stale assignees (e.g., after reopen).\n    async fn clear_assignee(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush local bead changes to JSONL before release.\n    ///\n    /// Runs `br sync --flush-only` to ensure any local writes are persisted\n    /// to JSONL before attempting to release a bead. N child creations plus\n    /// N dependency links must commit together: otherwise a crash between the\n    /// `create` and the `dep add` (SIGKILL, OOM, pod eviction) leaves an orphaned\n    /// child with no dependency link, and the parent never unblocks — plan.md\n    /// Phase 5.3, Race 3.\n    ///\n    /// The parent is deliberately **not** closed: NEEDLE keeps a split parent\n    /// open/blocked while its children are worked.\n    ///\n    /// The default implementation performs the historical non-atomic sequence\n    /// (`create_bead` + `add_dependency`, one child at a time). Mock stores rely\n    /// on it, and bf-backed stores fall back to it when the atomic path is\n    /// unavailable. Backends that can run a transactional batch (bf) override\n    /// this to make the whole split crash-safe.\n    async fn split_bead(\n        &self,\n        parent_id: &BeadId,\n        children: &[NewChild<'_>],\n    ) -> Result<Vec<BeadId>> {\n        let mut created = Vec::with_capacity(children.len());\n        for child in children {\n            let child_id = self\n                .create_bead(child.title, child.body, child.labels)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create child bead: {}\", child.title))?;\n            self.add_dependency(&child_id, parent_id)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| {\n                    format!(\"failed to add dependency: {child_id} blocks {parent_id}\")\n                })?;\n            created.push(child_id);\n        }\n        Ok(created)\n    }\n\n    /// Remove a dependency link: `blocker_id` blocks `blocked_id`.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `br dep remove <blocked_id> <blocker_id>`.\n    async fn remove_dependency(&self, blocked_id: &BeadId, blocker_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Run `br doctor --repair` and return the report.\n    async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<RepairReport>;\n\n    /// Run `br doctor` (without `--repair`) to check database health.\n    ///\n    /// Returns warnings if any issues are detected, without attempting to fix them.\n    async fn doctor_check(&self) -> Result<RepairReport>;\n\n    /// Full database rebuild from the configured backend's durable checkpoint.\n    ///\n    /// The existing SQLite file set remains in a rollback backup until the\n    /// public backend import and doctor verification both succeed.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err` if rebuild or verification fails; the original database\n    /// is restored in that case.\n    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Check if this store has a valid bead store (i.e., has a `.beads/` directory).\n    ///\n    /// Returns `true` if the workspace contains a `.beads/` directory, `false` otherwise.\n    /// This is used by strands to distinguish between \"no home store configured\" (expected,\n    /// benign for roam-only workers) and \"home store is broken\" (unexpected, problem).\n    fn has_valid_store(&self) -> bool;\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(0));\n        let call_count_clone = Arc::clone(&call_count);\n\n        let result = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n            || {\n                let count = Arc::clone(&call_count_clone);\n                async move {\n                    count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    Ok::<_, io::Error>(b\"success\".to_vec())\n                }\n            },\n            5,\n            20,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        assert!(result.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(result.unwrap(), b\"success\".to_vec());\n let call_count_clone = Arc::clone(&call_count);\n\n        let result: std::io::Result<Vec<u8>> = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n            || {\n                let count = Arc::clone(&call_count_clone);\n                async move {\n                    let attempt = count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    if attempt < 2 {\n                        // Fail first 2 attempts with ETXTBSY\n                        Err::<_, io::Error>(make_etxtbsy_error())\n                    } else {\n                        Ok::<_, io::Error>(b\"success\".to_vec())\n                    }\n                }\n            },\n            5,\n            20,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        assert!(result.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(result.unwrap(), etxtbsy_retry_linear_timing() {\n        let call_count = Arc::new(AtomicU32::new(0));\n        let call_count_clone = Arc::clone(&call_count);\n\n        let start = Instant::now();\n\n        let result = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry(\n            || {\n                let count = Arc::clone(&call_count_clone);\n                async move {\n                    let attempt = count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);\n                    if attempt < 2 {\n                        Err::<_, io::Error>(make_etxtbsy_error())\n                    } else {\n                        Ok::<_, io::Error>(b\"success\".to_vec())\n                    }\n                }\n            },\n            5,\n            50,\n        )\n        .await;\n\n        let elapsed = start.elapsed();\n\n        assert!(result.is_ok());\n        assert_eq!(call_count.load(Ordering::SeqCst), 3); // 2 failures + 1 success\n\n        // With 2 retries at 50ms each, should take ~100ms\n let result = spawn_with_etxtbsy_retry_exponential(\n            || {\n                let count = Arc::clone(&call_count_clone);\n                async move {\n                    let attempt =
